Ensure that the scope of the accreditation of the official laboratories include those methods of laboratory analysis, test or diagnosis required to be used by the laboratory for analyses, tests or diagnoses of those pests included in the multi-annual survey programme, in line with Article 37(5)(a) of Regulation (EU) 2017/625.

Ensure that a statistically based annual survey programme based on the level of risk is established and implemented for Xylella fastidiosa, as required by Article 2(3) of Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1201. Ensure that this annual survey takes into account the European Food Safety Authority Guidelines for statistically sound and risk-based surveys of this pest in the survey design and the sampling scheme for all parts of Croatia, in line with Article 2(4) of the above EU Regulation.
Ensure that surveys for the presence of Bursaphelenchus xylophilus are annually carried out on vectors in line Article 2(1) of Implementing Decision 2012/535/EU.

Ensure that the CAs regularly review and, where appropriate, update their contingency plans in line with Article 25(4) of Regulations (EU) 2016/2031, and consult all relevant stakeholders in the process of keeping up to date the contingency plans in line with Article 25(1) of the same EU Regulation.

Ensure that procedures and/or arrangements are in place to ensure the effectiveness and appropriateness of official controls in the feed and seed areas as required by Article 5(1)(a) of Regulation (EU) 2017/625.

Ensure that official controls in the feed area; Are planned taking account of identified risks, including those associated with imported feed materials and their country of origin, in line with Article 9 of Regulation (EU) 2017/625, which requires official controls to be performed on a risk basis, Are completed as planned, specifically in relation to sampling and analysis of imported feed materials, so as to fully implement the planned risk-based control programme as required by Article 9 of Regulation (EC) No 2017/625.

Ensure that: All laboratories used for official controls on food, feed and seeds are designated, and that laboratories are only designated if they have the expertise, equipment and infrastructure required to carry out the required analyses on samples as required by Article 37(4)(a) of Regulation (EC) No 2017/625. All designated laboratories used for official controls on food and feed can deliver analysis results in a timely manner a s required by Article 37(4)(d) of Regulation (EU) 2017/625. All designated laboratories used for official controls on seeds are accredited in accordance with the EN ISO/IEC 17025 standard for the required analysis as required by Article 37(4)(e) of Regulation (EU) 2017/625. All designated laboratories used for official controls on seeds use analytical methods complying with internationally recognised rules or protocols or methods developed and recommended by the EU Reference Laboratory (EURL), where these methods exist, a s required by Article 34(2)(a) of Regulation (EU) 2017/625. The designation of laboratories used for official controls on food, feed and seed complies with Article 37(3) of Regulation (EC) No 2017/625.

Ensure that all feed samples are analysed for all GM events, so as to effectively verify compliance with Article 4 of Regulation (EC) No 1830/2003, i.e. to verify that all feed materials used in feeds not labelled as containing GM, contain either no GMOs, or contain GMOs at levels less than or equal to 0.9%.

At a national strategic level; Ensure that the sampling and analysis programme for GMOs in seeds is reviewed and updated to reflect all identified risks as required by Article 9 of Regulation (EU) 2017/625, so that it meets the requirements of Article 4(5) of Directive 2001/18/EC. Ensure that the legal criteria to determine compliance/non-compliance of seed samples is reviewed and updated so as to provide a clear legal basis in the case of non-compliances under Article 4(5) of Directive 2001/18/EC.

At an operational level; Ensure that in all cases of non-compliances related to seeds, that the CAs undertake actions to determine the origin and extent of the non-compliance as required by Article 138(1) of Regulation (EU) 2017/625. Ensure that the CAs consider the outcome of these investigations as a risk factor when selecting seed lots for official controls in line with Article 9 of Regulation (EU) 2017/625.

Ensure that the Central Competent Authorities (in the context of the overall planning of controls on seeds) and Regional/Local Competent Authorities (in the context of determining which operators and seed lots to target for sampling under their official controls) seek, and take account of, results of own controls that have been performed by the operators, or by a third party at their request, as required by Article 9(1)(d) of Regulation (EC) No 2017/625.

The competent authority should complete documented procedures so that they provide sufficient information and detailed instructions for staff, as required by Article 12(1) of Regulation (EU) 2017/625, to carry out official controls at the port, including inspections carried out according to Articles 19 and 20 of Regulation (EC) 1/2005.

The competent authority should take measures to ensure that inspections: · for the purpose of granting a certificate of approval or renewals of such approvals, and · on the loading of livestock vessels; are performed by a team of inspectors including at least an official veterinarian and a maritime expert, as required by Article 9 of Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/372 and Article 5 of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/842.

The competent authority should take measures to carry out official controls by an official veterinarian on board a livestock vessel during the entire first voyage following the approval of the livestock vessel and prior to the renewal of such approval, as required by Article 10(1) of Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/372.
To ensure that official controls consistently verify that feed business operator`s hazard analysis and critical control points (HACCP) plans are comprehensive and updated.

To ensure that official controls consistently verify that feed business operators meet the requirements for appropriate checks of the effectiveness of measures they have taken to minimise cross-contamination.

To ensure that the competent authorities' samplers have appropriate equipment (i.e. a mechanical or automatic divider necessary for preparation of final sam- ples in case of the control of constituents or substances likely to be distributed non-uniformly in feed), and consistently apply sampling techniques ensuring official samples' legal and technical validity.

To ensure by established procedures and documentation that the competent au- thorities may only designate a laboratory which fulfil the requirements as an official laboratory for the analysis of feed samples.

To ensure that, in the event of established non-compliance(s), the competent authority consistently ensures that feed business operator remedies the non- compliance(s) and prevents its further occurrences.

To ensure that official controls consistently verify that feed business operators meet the requirements for appropriate checks of the effectiveness of measures they have taken to minimise cross-contamination.

To ensure that the competent authorities' samplers have appropriate equipment (i.e. a mechanical or automatic divider necessary for preparation of final samples in case of the control of constituents or substances likely to be distributed non-uniformly in feed), and consistently apply sampling techniques ensuring official samples' legal and technical validity.

To ensure that official controls by the State Inspectorate are capable of verifying that feed business operators meet the requirements for appropriate and regular checks of the effectiveness of mixing (homogeneity).
To ensure that the test results interpretation approach for determining sampling- related non-compliances does take into account all of the relevant factors set out in the legislation.

To ensure that establishments are approved by the competent authority for the activities concerned only if the food business operator has demonstrated that it fully complies with the relevant requirements of food law, as required by Article 148.3 of Regulation (EU) 2017/625, and that the food business operators' obligation to notify any significant change in the approved activities is enforced, in order for the competent authority to always have up-to-date information on establishments, as required by Article 6.2 of Regulation (EC) No 852/2004..

To ensure, as required by Article 5(1)(e) of Regulation (EU) 2017/625, that the local competent authorities have, or have access to, a sufficient number of suitably qualified and experienced staff so that official controls and other official activities can be performed efficiently and effectively.
To ensure that the competent authority takes the required enforcement action when it identifies non-compliances, as required by Article 138.1 of Regulation (EU) 2017/625.

To comply with Article 18(1) of Regulation (EU) 2017/625, the CAs need to enhance the effectiveness of official controls aimed at verifying that FBOs fulfil their obligations, as specified in Article 5 of Regulation (EC) No 852/2004 and Article 3 of Regulation (EC) No 2073/2005. This includes, but is not limited to, verifying that FBOs, applying arrangements based on national guides to good hygiene practices, have adequate procedures based on HACCP principles to effectively manage microbiological risks related to ready-to-eat meat products.

In order to comply with Article 1 of Regulation (EC) No 2073/2005, the CAs should improve the effectiveness of official controls aimed at verifying that FBOs' own-check sampling programmes comply with the sampling plans laid down in Chapters 1 and 2 of Annex I to Regulation (EC) No 2073/2005.

In order to meet the requirements of Article 148 (3) of Regulation (EU) 2017/625, the CAs should ensure that establishments are approved for the activities concerned only if the food business operator has demonstrated that it complies with the relevant requirements of food law.

In order to perform their duties competently and in a consistent manner, the CCA should ensure, in line with the provisions of point 4 of Article 5 of Regulation (EU) 2017/625, that the official control staff receive the necessary additional training and support, for carrying out their control duties in establishments producing meat products. In particular, the CCA should provide the control staff involved in official controls of meat products establishments producing RTE foods with training and guidance (as necessary): · on the relevant requirements of Regulation (EC) No 2073/2005, and · on the requirements related to the official controls on FBOs' procedures based on HACCP principles. The CAs should verify that FBOs fulfil their obligations, as specified in Article 5 of Regulation (EC) No 852/2004 and Article 3 of Regulation (EC) No 2073/2005. This includes verifying the adequacy of procedures based on HACCP principles to effectively manage microbiological risks related to ready-to-eat meat products and ensuring that the physico-chemical evaluation of these products, to assess their ability to support Listeria monocytogenes growth, is conducted correctly.

The CAs should have adequate arrangements in place to ensure the effectiveness of official controls, as required by Article 5(1)(a) of Regulation (EU) 2017/625, in order to comply with Article 18(a) of the same Regulation for those controls aimed at verifying that FBOs meet the obligations outlined in Article 5 of Regulation (EC) No 852/2004 and provide assurances that their procedures based on HACCP principles are adequate. Particular attention should be given to · hazard identification and assessment; · strategies necessary to effectively manage microbiological risks associated with RTE meat products; · additional training of official staff, in accordance with their needs, to carry out their control duties in establishments producing meat products and meat preparations; · verification of the effectiveness of official controls through staff supervision following the aforementioned traini

In order to comply with Article 1 of Regulation (EC) No 2073/2005, the CAs should improve the effectiveness of official controls aimed at verifying that FBOs fulfil their obligations, as specified in Articles 3(2), and 5(2) of the same regulation. In particular, the verification that the food safety criteria applicable throughout the shelf-life of the products can be met under reasonably foreseeable conditions of distribution, storage and use and also verification that environmental sampling for Listeria monocytogenes is conducted correctly.
To ensure that official controls in ABP processing plants are effective in assessing operators' validation of their processing methods.

To ensure that comparative assessments are conducted for the authorisation of PPPs containing active substances that are candidates for substitution. This is to comply with Articles 50(4) of Regulation (EC) No. 1107/2009.
To ensure that emergency authorisations are immediately notified to the Com- mission and Member States. This is to comply with Article 53 of Regulation (EC) No. 1107/2009.

To ensure that the frequency of inspections at operators is decided upon using objective criteria that consider the risk of inappropriate PPP usage and the results of monitoring programmes as necessary. This is to comply with Article 9(1) and 24(1) and (2) of Regulation (EU) 2017/625. Recommendation is based upon conclusions Nos 55 and 56.

To define conditions and establish criteria for when prior notice to agricultural users would be necessary and duly justified for the official controls to be carried out. This is to comply with Article 9 (4) of Regulation (EU) 2017/625.
To define and implement measures and criteria for the withdrawal of training certificates provided to users, distributors and advisors. This is to comply with Article 5(2) of Directive 2008/128/EC.

To ensure the reliability and relevance of PPP analyses, and in particular that: - - The laboratory conducting the analysis is accredited to ISO/IEC 17025. - - Samples of PPPs are analysed to determine the presence of unacceptable co- formulants set out in Annex III to Regulation (EC) No 1107/2009 and the con- tent of impurities whose maximum content is established in the approval of rele- vant active substances, as referred to Article 6(b) of the same Regulation. This is to comply with Articles 37(4)(e) and 24(1) of Regulation (EU) 2017/625. Recommendation is based upon conclusions No 65.

To ensure the quality, consistency and effectiveness of official controls, in par- ticular that: - - Information and checklists provided to inspectors cover the verification of all relevant aspects of compliance of operators with articles 55, 65 and 67 of Regulation (EC) No 1107/2009. - - There is supervision of the inspectors, to identify and correct any weakness- es in their performance. This is to comply with Articles 4(2)(a), 5 (1)(a) and (b), 12(1) and 14(b)(iv) of Regulation (EU) 2017/625. Recommendation is based upon conclusions Nos 33,34, 85 and 97. to 75 and 89 to 93.

To ensure that unacceptable co-formulants, as defined by Article 27 of Regulation (EC) No 1107/2009, and impurities subject to conditions and restrictions, as defined by Article 6(b) of Regulation (EU) 1107/2009, are covered by the accreditation scope of a laboratory designated to carry out formulation analyses of PPPs, and that they are included in the official controls as laid down by Article 24(1) of Regulation (EU) 2017/625.

To ensure that controls on manufacturers verify, for PPPs placed on the market in Slovenia, compliance with the authorisation requirement regarding the source of production of active substances, safeners, and synergists, as stipulated in Article 29(1)(a) and (b) of Regulation (EC) No 1107/2009, as well as the movement within Slovenia and subsequent sale at the destination, of PPPs intended for use in another EU Member State or a third country, as stipulated in Article 29(2)(c) and (d) of the same Regulatio

To put in place appropriate methods or techniques, according to article 14 of Regulation (EU) 2017/625, in order to verify that the sale of PPPs authorised for professional use are restricted to individuals holding a training certificate, as laid down by Article 6(2) of Directive 2009/128/EC.
To consider the results of monitoring programmes as necessary when determining the frequency of the risk-based inspections. This is to comply with Article 24 (2)(a) of Regulation (EU) 2017/625.

To ensure that: · The official controls include all PPP operators in the chain of marketing and use of PPPs as required by Article 9(1) of Regulation (EU) 2017/625, · The Competent Authority keeps or has access to an up-to-date lists of operators as required by Article 10(2) of Regulation (EU) 2017/625. Recommendation is based upon conclusions No 55

Ensure that official controls on the marketing and use of PPPs are performed regularly, with appropriate frequency and to ensure that the frequency of inspections at operators is decided upon using objective criteria that consider the risk of inappropriate PPP usage and the results of monitoring programmes as necessary. To define conditions and establish criteria for when prior notice to operators marketing and using PPPs would be necessary and duly justified for the official controls to be carried out. This is to comply with Article 9 (4) of Regulation (EU) 2017/625.
